text: There is a certain 'procede noble et galant', which should always be observed among the ministers of powers even at war with each other, which will always turn out to the advantage of the ablest, who will in those conversations find, or make, opportunities of throwing out, or of receiving useful hints.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CCXV, to his son, Bath, December 31, 1757
